description: The same key, on a screen lit three different ways. The plate is `#00b140` in three vertical bands -- full light, 42% and 20% -- with one warm off-white block straddling all three, and the whole of what this fixture asserts is that one key takes all three bands. They are the same colour and three brightnesses of it, which is what a real screen is: brighter where the lights point, darker in the subject's shadow. Expect a blue frame with the block standing on it, and no seam anywhere the bands met. What a wrong render looks like: a keyer measuring distance in RGB rather than with the light divided out passes the first band and fails the other two, so the left third comes back blue and the middle and right thirds come back green and darker green -- exactly the shape of the bug, since a screen is always brightest where the lights are pointed. Two dark bands with a keyed left third is that bug; three keyed bands with a visible seam between them means the ramp is being reached differently in each, which a spatially uniform key cannot do.
